organizingIdeas.title: Matter
organizingIdeas.statement: Understandings of the physical world are deepened by investigating matter and energy.

organizingIdeas.title: Energy
organizingIdeas.statement: Understandings of the physical world are deepened by investigating matter and energy.

guidingQuestions.question: Where do light and sound come from, and how do they move?

outcomes.outcome: Students investigate the behaviours of light and sound.

knowledge.text: Sound behaves in various ways, including
items: travelling in a straight line from its source
transferring from one object to another

knowledge.text: Sound is produced by vibrations of objects.
Vibration is a rapid back-and-forth movement.
Sources of sound can be natural or human-made, such as
items: vocal cords of humans and other animals

knowledge.text: Characteristics of sound include
items: volume, which can be described as quiet or loud
pitch, which can be described as high or low
duration, which can be described as short or long

organizingIdeas.title: Earth Systems
organizingIdeas.statement: Understandings of the living world, Earth, and space are deepened by investigating natural systems and their interactions.

guidingQuestions.question: How can Earth’s components and relationship to the Sun be understood?

outcomes.outcome: Students investigate Earth, its landforms, its bodies of water, and its relationship to the Sun.

knowledge.text: Components of Earth include
At this time, Earth is the only planet known to support life.
Scientists are looking for life on other planets and moons.

understanding.text: Earth consists of many components that support life.

skillsAndProcedures.text: Represent various components of Earth.
Discuss how the various components of Earth interact to support life.

small streams merging to form larger streams and rivers
streams and small rivers merging to form larger rivers

knowledge.text: A year is the length of time it takes Earth to revolve around the Sun.
A day is the length of time it takes Earth to rotate fully (on its axis).
Earth’s surface experiences day when it faces the Sun and night when it does not face the Sun.

understanding.text: Earth revolves around the Sun and rotates.

skillsAndProcedures.text: Describe the relationship between time and Earth revolving around the Sun.

organizingIdeas.title: Living Systems
organizingIdeas.statement: Understandings of the living world, Earth, and space are deepened by investigating natural systems and their interactions.

guidingQuestions.question: How do plants and animals live and grow?

outcomes.outcome: Students investigate the growth and development of plants and animals and consider their relationship to humans.

Some human behaviours can negatively affect plants and animals, such as
items: using up materials from nature that plants and animals need to live
introducing plants and other animals that are not native to the area

organizingIdeas.title: Computer Science
organizingIdeas.statement: Problem solving and scientific inquiry are developed through the knowledgeable application of creativity, design, and computational thinking.

organizingIdeas.title: Scientific Methods
organizingIdeas.statement: Investigation of the physical world is enhanced through the use of scientific methods that attempt to remove human biases and increase objectivity.

guidingQuestions.question: What methods and processes can be used in scientific investigation?

outcomes.outcome: Students examine investigation and explain how it is influenced by purpose.
